_schema.purpose: Audit verdicts for atoms in docs/roadmap/atomic/dag.json. THIS is where a verdict is recorded — never by editing a generated <ID>.md, which the next generator run discards.
_schema.keys: one per atom id; keys beginning with _ are documentation and are ignored

verdict.confirmed: every done_when clause was checked against the code and holds
verdict.partial: some done_when clauses hold and others do not — say which in notes
verdict.contradicted: the status recorded in dag.json disagrees with the code
verdict.unverifiable: cannot be settled in this repo (needs hardware, a paid key, or an owner action)
verdict.unaudited: the default for an atom nobody has checked; normally absent rather than written

fields.evidence: list of concrete artifacts checked — paths, symbols, test names, measured counts
fields.ui_validated: what was DRIVEN in the running product through real user interaction, or absent if nothing was
fields.notes: the reasoning, especially any clause that did NOT hold
fields.follow_ups: list of PRs or issues opened as a result

_schema.rule: A verdict is a claim about evidence, not a vote. `confirmed` requires naming what was checked; an atom whose evidence is only a path that pre-existed the work is `partial` at best — see tools/audit_landed_atoms.py on why path-only evidence scores TRIVIAL.

PR2-1.by: audit cycle 8 (PR2) — RAN the real CLI
evidence: tests/test_resilience_doctor.py passes (part of 152 tests passing across six PR2 modules)

`personalclaw doctor` against the validation home produces a genuinely tiered report: Dependencies / Project / Agent / Configuration / MCP Tools / Runtime / Vector Memory / Speech-to-Text / Provider Health / Connectivity, each capability carrying its own status glyph (✅ present, ⏹ not configured, 🔐 credential file mode, 🕐 timezone source)
every not-configured line names its own REMEDY rather than just reporting absence — 'pick an embedding model in Settings → Models', 'install an STT app or bind one in Settings → Models'
PR2-1.notes: Confirmed by running it, not by reading its test. Two observations recorded rather than filed, because both are plausibly deliberate and need the owner's judgement. (1) The headline is '✅ PersonalClaw is ready!' while Configuration reports 'chat model: (none bound)' — arguably right (the box IS ready; binding a model is a separate step the UI advertises), but a reader could take 'ready' as 'can think'. (2) Connectivity reports 'gateway: ✅ running (uptime 49h 42m)' for a home whose own gateway I started two hours earlier: it probes the CONFIGURED dashboard URL (port 10000) rather than the running instance, so with a runtime --port override it can attribute another instance's gateway to this home. Faithful to config, potentially misleading across homes. Neither is a defect I would file without a ruling.

WF2TAS-12.notes: 🪤 A NAME COLLISION NEARLY MADE THIS A CONTRADICTION — the fifth finding to collapse on inspection this audit. Searching for the enum returned `class Lifecycle` alive at workflows/workspace.py:71 and still used at :525, which reads exactly like a retirement that never happened. Reading it settles it: that enum is FOLDER lifecycles (TRANSIENT / TTL_STAGING / PERMANENT / IMMUTABLE), a filesystem staging concept whose docstring explains propose-don't-write enforcement. Same identifier, unrelated concept. There is also a separate LifecyclePhase in workflows/models.py. The lesson for the remaining plans: a retirement claim must be checked against what the surviving symbol MEANS, not against its name, or every reused word reads as a broken clean break.

KL-1.notes: 🪤 THIS NEARLY BECAME A FALSE 'DOES NOT PERSIST' FINDING, and the correction matters more than the verdict. After saving, `grep -rl` over the home found the title in NO file, and `find -newermt '-4 minutes'` reported NOTHING written. That reads exactly like a UI-only write. It was wrong: a page RELOAD re-fetched the item from the server, which is the decisive user-level test. My file probes were not measuring the right thing — the knowledge store is not a plain file under the paths I searched. Two lessons: a reload is a better persistence test than a file-mtime scan, and an absent grep hit is not an absent write.

RUA-4.notes: PARTIAL, and it produced the cycle's one real finding — issue #2735. The dashboard middleware that sets Cache-Control/Pragma/Expires and a detailed CSP sets NO frame-ancestors directive and NO X-Frame-Options anywhere in src/. frame-ancestors does not fall back to default-src, and frame-src is the opposite control, so nothing restricts who may frame the authenticated dashboard — in exactly the public-exposure scenario this atom hardens. The finding is strong because the project already holds the standard elsewhere: artifacts/deploy.py:109 sets frame-ancestors 'self' with a test asserting it at test_artifact_deploy_serve.py:344. Severity is genuinely reduced by SameSite=Lax (a cross-site frame carries no session cookie), and the issue says so rather than overstating; what remains is login-page UI redressing and the deliberate ?token= path, which SameSite does not cover. FILED rather than fixed because the change would break any legitimate cross-origin embedder (Electron shell, preview panes) and that compatibility check is the part that makes it not a ten-minute job. ARCC's Secure HTTP Headers guidance also asks for Referrer-Policy and X-Content-Type-Options on ALL responses; both exist only on specific artifact/file responses here, and #2735 covers promoting them. I did NOT verify the TOTP or enrollment-code clauses — both need a provisioned credential, same blocker as RUA-3.
